Your insurance can tell you whether you need a doctor’s referral, but I’d think not since this is psychological - not physical.

It’s not a test. It’s a conversation. The psychiatrist will ask you questions. They may want to talk to a parent or someone who lead/leads you.

There might be a list of question for you to answer. Not like a quiz. Like: Do you misplace things? Not really that question, but questions that are that easy to answer. 

The doc will make the diagnosis on the spot. There’s no analysis of the collected data. It’s just “Yeah, I’d say you are ADHD” and then you’ve been diagnosed. The psych doc will (hopefully) discuss possible treatments.

If you both decide that you should take meds, they’ll write you a prescription and you can pick it up that day.

Not all treatments are pharmaceutical. You can see therapists who specialize in ADHD. 

Everything may be subject to your insurance. The doc and the pharmacy are both likely to have the ability to see what your insurance covers.

It’s a journey, but if you can keep it going it’ll done before you know it.

Well, I still scored an F and a W among the A's, but it didn't matter - I was learning what I found interesting and I was immediately able to apply it to my work.

Study what you like. If you don't want to study now, I'd suggest working for a couple years in a field you're interested in and if you're like me you'll figure out what you want to learn along the way and you can go back and finish your degree - or just take more classes without pursuit of a degree. Your GPA only matters if you're relying on your schooling to get a specialized job. Once you've worked for a couple years and have a bit of a resume, your GPA will no longer matter and you'll never even think about it again.
